scenes.tts: If Sperry was right, the target itself carries a cue. Can we ask an axon to read it?
scenes.visual: Title card: Reading the Slope. A target strip with a question mark over it.
scenes.narration: If Sperry was right, the target itself carries a cue. Can we ask an axon to read it?

scenes.tts: In nineteen eighty-seven, Friedrich Bonhoeffer's group built a striped carpet.
scenes.caption: In 1987, Friedrich Bonhoeffer's group built a striped carpet.
scenes.visual: Label: Walter, Bonhoeffer and colleagues, 1987. A dish seen from above.
scenes.narration: In 1987, Friedrich Bonhoeffer's group built a striped carpet.

scenes.tts: Membranes from the front and back of chick tectum lay in alternating narrow lanes.
scenes.visual: Alternating lanes appear: anterior lanes pale, posterior lanes dark. Labels: anterior, posterior.
scenes.narration: Membranes from the front and back of chick tectum lay in alternating narrow lanes.

scenes.tts: A strip of retina lay across them, so each growing axon met border after border.
scenes.visual: A strip of retina lies across the lanes; axons begin to grow out over the borders.
scenes.narration: A strip of retina lay across them, so each growing axon met border after border.

scenes.tts: Where will axons from the temporal retina grow?
scenes.visual: Temporal axons poised at the lane edge. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Where will axons from the temporal retina grow?

scenes.tts: Temporal axons grew along the front lanes and stayed off the back ones. Nasal axons grew on both.
scenes.visual: Temporal axons run only on pale anterior lanes. A second panel: nasal axons cross both kinds.
scenes.narration: Temporal axons grew along the front lanes and stayed off the back ones. Nasal axons grew on both.

scenes.tts: On either membrane alone, both grew well. So the back membrane was not simply a poor surface.
scenes.visual: Two small dishes, each a single membrane type; axons grow well on both.
scenes.narration: On either membrane alone, both grew well. So the back membrane was not simply a poor surface.

scenes.tts: Now heat the back membranes first. What will the temporal axons do?
scenes.visual: The dark posterior lanes are heated before the assay. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Now heat the back membranes first. What will the temporal axons do?

scenes.tts: The avoidance vanished. An attractant on the unheated front lanes would have kept it.
scenes.visual: Temporal axons now grow on both lane types. The pale anterior lanes are marked: not heated.
scenes.narration: The avoidance vanished. An attractant on the unheated front lanes would have kept it.

scenes.tts: So the cue is a heat-sensitive repellent at the back of the tectum.
scenes.visual: The posterior lanes glow. On screen: heat-sensitive posterior repellent.
scenes.narration: So the cue is a heat-sensitive repellent at the back of the tectum.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-five, one paper found a repellent at the back of the tectum, now called eff-rin A five.
scenes.caption: In 1995, one paper found a repellent at the back of the tectum, now called ephrin-A5.
scenes.visual: Two journal pages side by side, dated 1995. Left label: ephrin-A5, purified. Right label: ephrin-A2 gradient mapped (cloned 1994).
scenes.narration: In 1995, one paper found a repellent at the back of the tectum, now called ephrin-A5.

scenes.tts: A second paper mapped the gradient of eff-rin A two, which had been cloned the year before.
scenes.caption: A second paper mapped the gradient of ephrin-A2, which had been cloned the year before.
scenes.visual: The right-hand page highlights a gradient across the tectum. Label: ephrin-A2, cloned 1994; gradient reported 1995.
scenes.narration: A second paper mapped the gradient of ephrin-A2, which had been cloned the year before.

scenes.tts: Eff-rin A rises from front to back across the tectum. Its receptor, Eff A, runs the opposite way, high in temporal retina.
scenes.caption: Ephrin-A rises from front to back across the tectum. Its receptor, EphA, runs the opposite way, high in temporal retina.
scenes.visual: Two opposite slopes: ephrin-A on the target rising front to back; EphA on the retina, highest at the temporal end. Orientation throughout: retina strip on the left, nasal at top, temporal at bottom; target strip on the right with anterior (front) on the left of its own bar.
scenes.narration: Ephrin-A rises from front to back across the tectum. Its receptor, EphA, runs the opposite way, high in temporal retina.

scenes.tts: Why does more receptor mean ending at the front? Take toy numbers. Repulsion is the receptor level times the local ligand.
scenes.visual: On screen: toy numbers, not measured. EphA 1, 2, 3 units. Ephrin-A rising in a straight line from 1 at the front edge (x = 0) to 3 at the back edge (x = 1); label: linear toy gradient. Repulsion = EphA × ephrin-A. Limit = 3.
scenes.narration: Why does more receptor mean ending at the front? Take toy numbers. Repulsion is the receptor level times the local ligand.

scenes.tts: Each axon enters at the front and grows back. It keeps its branches where the repulsion reaches the limit.
scenes.visual: Three axons with meters labelled EphA × ephrin-A begin at the anterior edge and move back.
scenes.narration: Each axon enters at the front and grows back. It keeps its branches where the repulsion reaches the limit.

scenes.tts: Three axons carry low, middle and high receptor. Which reaches the limit first?
scenes.visual: The three meters pause. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Three axons carry low, middle and high receptor. Which reaches the limit first?

scenes.tts: The axon with the most receptor hits the limit first, at the front edge. The axon with the least ends at the back.
scenes.visual: Meters stop: EphA 3 at ephrin 1 (x = 0, front edge); EphA 2 at ephrin 1.5 (x = 0.25, a quarter of the way back); EphA 1 at ephrin 3 (x = 1, back edge). Label: toy endpoint rule, not a full mechanism.
scenes.narration: The axon with the most receptor hits the limit first, at the front edge. The axon with the least ends at the back.

scenes.tts: One correction. In chick and mouse, axons first overshoot their zone, then sprout side branches.
scenes.visual: One axon overshoots toward the back, then sprouts side branches along its length.
scenes.narration: One correction. In chick and mouse, axons first overshoot their zone, then sprout side branches.

scenes.tts: Eff-rin A keeps branches from forming and surviving behind the right zone. The overshooting part is later removed.
scenes.caption: Ephrin-A keeps branches from forming and surviving behind the right zone. The overshooting part is later removed.
scenes.visual: Branches behind the right zone fade; the overshooting tip retracts. A tuft remains at the right zone.
scenes.narration: Ephrin-A keeps branches from forming and surviving behind the right zone. The overshooting part is later removed.

scenes.tts: So where an axon stops means where it keeps its branches, its termination zone.
scenes.visual: Label on the remaining tuft: termination zone.
scenes.narration: So where an axon stops means where it keeps its branches, its termination zone.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: more receptor, less ligand. In the toy, two opposite slopes put the axons in order.
scenes.visual: On screen: more receptor, less ligand. The two slopes with five axons in order between them. Small label: toy model; comparison among axons comes next.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: more receptor, less ligand. In the toy, two opposite slopes put the axons in order.
